CHEM 100.title: Foundations of Chemistry
CHEM 100.description: Atomic and molecular properties, chemical reactions, bonding, nomenclature, kinetics, equilibrium processes, acids and bases, oxidation and reduction. Intended for students who do not receive a satisfactory score on the UBC Chemistry Basic Skills Test, and need to establish a foundation of chemistry skills before proceeding to other first year chemistry courses. .

children.raw: Not open to students with credit for

CHEM 100.prerequisiteText: Not open to students with credit for Chemistry 12. Permission of the department head

CHEM 110.title: Structure, Bonding and Equilibrium in Chemistry (Lecture)
CHEM 110.description: Fundamentals of bonding theories, structural chemistry and equilibrium with applications relevant to modern society. .

CHEM 110.prerequisiteText: Not open to students with credit for Chemistry 12. A satisfactory score on the UBC Chemistry Basic Skills Test

CHEM 111.title: Structure, Bonding, and Equilibrium in Chemistry
CHEM 111.description: Fundamentals of bonding theories, structural chemistry and equilibrium with applications relevant to modern society.

CHEM 115.title: Introductory Chemical Laboratory I
CHEM 115.description: An introduction to the principles and techniques of the chemistry laboratory.

CHEM 120.title: Structure and Bonding in Chemistry (Lecture)
CHEM 120.description: Fundamentals of bonding theories, structural chemistry, with applications relevant to modern society. .

CHEM 121.title: Structure and Bonding in Chemistry
CHEM 121.description: Fundamentals of bonding theories and structural chemistry, with applications relevant to modern society.

CHEM 123.title: Thermodynamics, Kinetics and Organic Chemistry
CHEM 123.description: Fundamentals of chemical reactivity: thermodynamics; kinetics; organic chemistry, including stereochemistry; applications relevant to modern society.

CHEM 130.title: Thermodynamics, Kinetics and Organic Chemistry (Lecture)
CHEM 130.description: Fundamentals of chemical reactivity: thermodynamics; kinetics; organic chemistry, including stereochemistry; applications relevant to modern society.
CHEM 130.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM 110, CHEM 111, CHEM 120, CHEM 121, CHEM 141

CHEM 135.title: Introductory Chemical Laboratory II
CHEM 135.description: An introduction to the principles and techniques of the chemistry laboratory.
CHEM 135.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM 111, CHEM 115, CHEM 121, CHEM 141

CHEM 141.title: Chemical Bonding, Molecular Structure and Properties for Lab Sciences
CHEM 141.description: Bonding theories, their predictions, experimental tests, and consequences regarding chemical structure and observable properties. Applications relevant to modern society are emphasized. For students interested in lab-focused sciences such as Chemistry, Physics, Biochemistry, Microbiology and related disciplines. Restricted to students in the Faculty of Science.

CHEM 154.title: Chemistry for Engineering
CHEM 154.description: Chemical bonding, properties of matter. Chemical thermodynamics with applications to phase equilibria, aqueous equilibria and electrochemistry. Processes at surfaces.

CHEM 203.title: Introduction to Organic Chemistry
CHEM 203.description: Structure, bonding and physical properties of aliphatic and aromatic compounds; mechanistic analysis of chemical reactivity of common functional groups with a focus on carbon-heteroatom bond formation; functional group interconversion and oxidation/reduction reactions. Only open to students in Chemistry or Biochemistry specializations.
CHEM 203.prerequisiteText: Either (a) CHEM 123 or (b) all of CHEM 130, CHEM 135 or (c) SCIE 001

CHEM 205.title: Physical Chemistry
CHEM 205.description: Chemical kinetics and thermodynamics and spectroscopy useful in biological, medical, agricultural, earth, and related sciences.
CHEM 205.prerequisiteText: Either (a) SCIE_V 001 or (b) one of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, MATH_O 100 and one of CHEM_V 130, CHEM_V 123, CHEM_V 154

CHEM 208.title: Coordination Chemistry
CHEM 208.description: Fundamental concepts and principles governing bonding and reactivity of coordination complexes: ligand field theory; symmetry and point groups; frontier molecular orbital theory. .

CHEM 210.title: Introduction to Chemical Analysis (Lecture)
CHEM 210.description: Quantitative chemical analysis; chemical and physical principles of spectrophotometry, potentiometry, and chromatography.

CHEM 211.title: Introduction to Chemical Analysis
CHEM 211.description: Quantitative chemical analysis; chemical and physical principles of spectrophotometry, potentiometry, and chromatography. .
CHEM 211.prerequisiteText: Either (a) CHEM_V 123 or (b) all of CHEM_V 130, CHEM_V 135 or (c) SCIE_V 001

CHEM 213.title: Organic Chemistry
CHEM 213.description: Spectroscopy of organic compounds. Mechanistic analysis of chemical reactivity of common functional groups with a focus on carbon-carbon bond formation; functional group interconversion. Preference will be given to students in Chemistry or Biochemistry specializations.

CHEM 213.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of CHEM_V 203, CHEM_V 223, CHEM_O 203 or (b) a score of 76% or higher in CHEM_V 233 or CHEM_O 213

CHEM 215.title: Introductory Analytical Chemical Laboratory
CHEM 215.description: An introduction to the principles and techniques in the analytical chemistry laboratory.
CHEM 215.prerequisiteText: CHEM 210 and one of CHEM 123, CHEM 135

CHEM 218.title: Fundamentals of Reactivity in Inorganic Chemistry
CHEM 218.description: Chemical reactivity of inorganic systems: oxidation/reduction chemistry; multiply-bonded systems; main group chemistry. .

CHEM 223.title: Introduction to Organic Chemistry (Lecture)
CHEM 223.description: Structure, bonding and physical properties of aliphatic and aromatic compounds; mechanistic analysis of chemical reactivity of common functional groups with a focus on carbon-heteroatom bond formation; functional group interconversion and oxidation/reduction reactions. Only open to students in Chemistry or Biochemistry specializations. Students should consult the Credit Exclusion List for credit exclusions relating to second-year organic chemistry courses.

CHEM 225.title: Introductory Synthetic Chemical Laboratory
CHEM 225.description: An introduction to the principles and techniques in the synthetic organic and inorganic chemistry laboratory.

CHEM 233.title: Organic Chemistry for the Biological Sciences
CHEM 233.description: Reactions and properties of carbonyl compounds, carbohydrates, amino acids, nucleic acids.

CHEM 235.title: Organic Chemistry Laboratory
CHEM 235.description: Techniques of organic chemistry. To be taken in conjunction with, or in the term following, CHEM_V 233.

CHEM 245.title: Intermediate Synthetic Chemistry Laboratory
CHEM 245.description: Techniques in synthetic organic and inorganic chemistry. Open only to students in Chemistry or Biochemistry specializations. .
CHEM 245.prerequisiteText: Either (a) CHEM_V 203 or (b) all of CHEM_V 223, CHEM_V 225 or (c) all of CHEM_V 233, CHEM_V 235

CHEM 250.title: Inorganic Chemistry for Engineers
CHEM 250.description: Chemistry of selected groups of inorganic compounds, considered in relation to industrial processes.
CHEM 250.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, CHEM 154, SCIE 001

CHEM 251.title: Physical Chemistry for Engineers
CHEM 251.description: States of matter, properties of gases, phase diagrams. Elementary chemical thermodynamics and kinetics. Reaction equilibria.
CHEM 251.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, CHEM 154, SCIE 001

CHEM 260.title: Organic Chemistry for Engineers
CHEM 260.description: A description of the properties and reactions of organic compounds.
CHEM 260.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, CHEM 154, SCIE 001

CHEM 300.title: Communicating Chemistry
CHEM 300.description: Effective argumentation and communication skills in chemistry. Only open to students in a Chemistry specialization. .

CHEM 301.title: Aqueous Environmental Chemistry
CHEM 301.description: Properties and composition of natural waters, including gas and solid equilibria, pH and acidification, redox chemistry, complexation, corrosion, ion exchange, colloids and microbial transformations.
CHEM 301.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, CHBE 220. and Third year standing

CHEM 302.title: Atmospheric Environmental Chemistry
CHEM 302.description: Introduction to structure, composition and chemical processes occurring in Earth's atmosphere, including interactions with solar radiation, stratospheric ozone layer, photochemical smog and acid rain.
CHEM 302.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, CHBE 220. and Third year standing

CHEM 304.title: Fundamentals of Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics
CHEM 304.description: Principles of chemical thermodynamics; introduction to statistical mechanics; phase equilibria; electrochemistry.
CHEM 304.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM_V 123, CHEM_V 130 and one of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253

CHEM 305.title: Biophysical Chemistry
CHEM 305.description: Diffusion and transport phenomena; interaction of radiation and matter. Methods for determining molecular weight, size, and shape of molecules in solution.

children.raw: a score of 76% or higher in

CHEM 305.prerequisiteText: One of MATH 200, MATH 217, MATH 226, MATH 253 and either (a) a score of 76% or higher in CHEM 205 or (b) CHEM 304 or (c) PHYS 203

CHEM 311.title: Instrumental Analytical Chemistry
CHEM 311.description: Theory, design, and application of instrumental methods of chemical analysis including spectroscopy, mass spectrometry, electroanalysis, and chemical separations.

CHEM 312.title: Introduction to Quantum Mechanics and Spectroscopy
CHEM 312.description: Principles of quantum mechanics; atomic wavefunctions; angular momentum; spin; atomic term symbols.
CHEM 312.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM_V 123, SCIE_V 001 and one of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253

CHEM 313.title: Advanced Organic Chemistry for the Life Sciences
CHEM 313.description: Chemistry of organic substances having particular relevance to the life sciences.

CHEM 315.title: Chemistry Integrated Laboratory I
CHEM 315.description: Principles and techniques of modern chemistry applied by integrating experiments chosen from organic, inorganic, physical, and analytical chemistry.
CHEM 315.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM 211, CHEM 215 and all of CHEM 213, CHEM 245

CHEM 318.title: Principles of Catalysis
CHEM 318.description: Fundamental aspects of chemical catalysis: kinetic models; catalytic processes in biochemistry and industry; emerging topics in catalysis. .

CHEM 319.title: Practical Skills for Chemical Research
CHEM 319.description: The nature of scientific research; practical skills for chemical research; communicating science. Restricted to Honours students with third year standing and, with permission of the department Head, to Major students with satisfactory third year standing. .

CHEM 325.title: Integrated Chemistry Laboratory I
CHEM 325.description: Principles and techniques of modern chemistry applied by integrating experiments chosen from organic, inorganic, physical, and analytical chemistry. Open only to students in Chemistry specializations.
CHEM 325.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM 211, CHEM 215 and all of CHEM 208, CHEM 213, CHEM 245

CHEM 327.title: Introduction to Materials Chemistry
CHEM 327.description: Basic principles of materials chemistry: classification; nomenclature; synthetic methods; characterization. .
CHEM 327.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM_V 208, CHEM_V 250 and one of CHEM_V 203, CHEM_V 223, CHEM_V 233, CHEM_V 260

CHEM 329.title: Research Ethics and Data Analysis Skills
CHEM 329.description: Research ethics; data analysis skills for chemical research. Restricted to Honours students with third year standing and, with permission of the department Head, to Major students with satisfactory third year standing. .

CHEM 330.title: Advanced Organic Chemistry
CHEM 330.description: Application of carbonyl group chemistry, cyclization reactions, conformational analysis and rearrangement reactions in organic synthesis.

CHEM 335.title: Chemistry Integrated Laboratory II
CHEM 335.description: Further development of principles and techniques of modern chemistry applied by integrating experiments chosen from organic, inorganic, physical, and analytical chemistry.

CHEM 341.title: Global Challenges: A Chemical Perspective
CHEM 341.description: Importance of chemistry in society. Detailed case studies drawn from modern chemistry: human health, energy, commodity chemicals, materials, green chemistry, agriculture.
CHEM 341.prerequisiteText: one of CHEM_V 203, CHEM_V 211, CHEM_V 223, CHEM_V 233, CHEM_V 260

CHEM 345.title: Integrated Chemistry Laboratory II
CHEM 345.description: Further development of principles and techniques of modern chemistry applied by integrating experiments chosen from organic, inorganic, physical, and analytical chemistry. Open only to students in Chemistry Major or Honours specializations.

CHEM 355.title: Chemistry Integrated Laboratory
CHEM 355.description: Principles and techniques of modern chemistry for students in Combined Major in Science or a Minor in Chemistry integrating experiments from organic, inorganic, physical and analytical chemistry.

CHEM 398.title: Co-operative Work Placement I
CHEM 398.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Taken during the winter term of the third year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Chemistry.

CHEM 399.title: Co-operative Work Placement II
CHEM 399.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Taken during the summer following the third year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Chemistry.

CHEM 401.title: Principles of Spectroscopy
CHEM 401.description: Rotational, vibrational, electronic and magnetic resonance spectroscopy and associated techniques; group theory.
CHEM 401.prerequisiteText: One of MATH_V 111, MATH_V 131, MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223 and one of CHEM_V 312, PHYS_V 304

CHEM 402.title: Diffraction Methods
CHEM 402.description: Crystal structures; point and space groups; X-ray diffraction, neutron diffraction, electron diffraction of gases and surfaces.

CHEM 403.title: Surface Chemistry and Surface Analysis
CHEM 403.description: Surfaces and phenomena occurring at surfaces and interfaces: adsorption, thermodynamic treatments, technological applications. Methods for characterization and modification of surfaces. Dynamic electrochemistry and its application to understanding fuel cells.
CHEM 403.prerequisiteText: CHEM_V 304 and one of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253

CHEM 404.title: Computational Chemistry
CHEM 404.description: Application of numerical techniques to study chemical systems; molecular simulation. Prior computer programming experience is not required. .
CHEM 404.prerequisiteText: Either (a) SCIE_V 001 or (b) one of CHEM_V 123, CHEM_V 130, CHEM_V 154 and one of PHYS_V 106, PHYS_V 107, PHYS_V 108, PHYS_V 117, PHYS_V 118, PHYS_V 170 and one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121 and Third-year standing

CHEM 405.title: Biophysical Chemistry
CHEM 405.description: Interactions of macromolecules in solution: ligand, antibody and ion binding to macromolecules; thermodynamics of polymer solutions; excluded volume effects; phase separation; partition in two phase polymer solutions.

CHEM 406.title: Polymer Chemistry
CHEM 406.description: Structure and availability of monomers; Propagation mechanisms; synthesis of polymers with predetermined properties; measurement and interpretation of physical properties of polymers.
CHEM 406.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM 213, CHEM 260 and one of CHEM 205, CHEM 304, CHBE 220

CHEM 407.title: Statistical Mechanics in Chemistry
CHEM 407.description: Introductory concepts of statistical mechanics and statistical thermodynamics. Applications to chemistry with emphasis on understanding chemical reactivity.

CHEM 408.title: Chemical Dynamics
CHEM 408.description: Macroscopic and microscopic kinetics; photochemistry; theory of reaction rates; reaction cross sections, energy distributions, experimental methods.
CHEM 408.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM 304, PHYS 203 and one of CHEM 312, PHYS 304

CHEM 409.title: Astrochemistry
CHEM 409.description: Application of physical chemistry concepts and principles to the study of molecules in interstellar media and celestial bodies.

children.raw: with a minimum grade of 76% may be admitted with permission of the instructor

CHEM 409.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM 312, PHYS 304. Students with CHEM 205 with a minimum grade of 76% may be admitted with permission of the instructor

CHEM 410.title: Properties of Materials
CHEM 410.description: Electromagnetic, optical, thermal and mechanical properties, and chemical reactivity of solids; electrons in periodic systems: bands, zones; excitations: excitons, phonons, plasmons, polaritons; crystalline order and disorder; ionic conductivity.
CHEM 410.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM 304, PHYS 203 and one of CHEM 312, PHYS 304

CHEM 411.title: Synthesis and Chemistry of Natural Products
CHEM 411.description: Methods and tactics for the synthesis of biologically active natural products and analogs, particularly alkaloids, polyketides, steroids and terpenes.

CHEM 412.title: Electronic Structure of Atoms and Molecules
CHEM 412.description: Introduction to variational methods; many-electron systems; semi-empirical methods; perturbation theory; computational methods.
CHEM 412.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM_V 312, PHYS_V 304 and one of MATH_V 111, MATH_V 131, MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223

CHEM 413.title: Bioorganic Chemistry
CHEM 413.description: Enzyme catalysis; mechanistic enzymology; chemistry of cofactors; biosynthetic transformations; natural product biosynthesis; topics in chemical biology.

CHEM 414.title: Coordination Chemistry of the Transition Elements
CHEM 414.description: Molecular and electronic structures and reactivities of coordination compounds of the transition elements.

CHEM 416.title: Physical and Theoretical Organic Chemistry
CHEM 416.description: Energetics and catalysis in organic reactions. Pericyclic reactions. Substituent effects. Linear free energy relationships.

CHEM 417.title: Nuclear Chemistry and Radiochemistry
CHEM 417.description: Basic treatment of the nucleus, with analogy to concepts in chemistry. Nuclear stabilities and associated radioactive decay processes. Nuclear structure. Applications of radioisotopes in chemistry. The interaction of radiation with matter.
CHEM 417.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130. and Third year standing

CHEM 418.title: Organometallic Chemistry
CHEM 418.description: The chemistry of compounds containing organic groups directly bonded to metals and metalloids. Emphasis will be placed on the structure and bonding of the compounds and their use in synthetic chemistry.

CHEM 419.title: Establishing a Career in Chemical Research
CHEM 419.description: Current research and career perspectives in chemistry. Restricted to Honours students with fourth year standing and, with permission of the department Head, to Major students with satisfactory fourth year standing. .

CHEM 427.title: Applications of Materials Chemistry
CHEM 427.description: Contemporary materials chemistry, including design and synthesis of materials for energy, electronics, and health applications.

CHEM 430.title: Developments in Contemporary Chemistry
CHEM 430.description: A review of modern developments in general chemistry for teachers of Secondary School chemistry (Not for credit in the Faculty of Science). Course is offered periodically in extra-sessional sessions.

CHEM 434.title: Principles of Chemical Separation
CHEM 434.description: Unified theory of separation science; liquid and gas chromatography; capillary electrophoresis; electrochemical and spectroscopic detection; separation methods coupled with mass spectrometry and tandem mass spectrometry; biochemical applications.

CHEM 435.title: Bio-Inorganic Chemistry
CHEM 435.description: A discussion of the involvement of inorganic chemistry in biological systems. Chemistry of cations, metalloenzymes, and simpler model systems. Reactions of coordinated ligands, chemistry of sulfur and phosphorus.

CHEM 445.title: Projects in Experimental Chemistry
CHEM 445.description: Principles of experimental design, practice and problem solving in chemistry, including the opportunity to pursue projects in a research setting. Students cannot take both CHEM_V 445 and CHEM_V 449.

must have 4th-year class standing in a Chemistry Combined Major specialization

CHEM 445.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM_V 345, CHEM_V 335. Students satisfying the prerequisite requirement using CHEM_V 335 must have 4th-year class standing in a Chemistry Combined Major specialization

CHEM 448.title: Directed Studies in Chemistry
CHEM 448.description: Students will undertake an investigation of a specific topic as agreed upon by the student and the faculty supervisor. Open to third- and fourth-year chemistry students.

CHEM 449.title: Seminar and Thesis
CHEM 449.description: Original research work under the direction of a faculty member. Weekly seminar. Required of all Honours students. Open to Majors students with a satisfactory standing and permission of the department head. Students cannot take both CHEM_V 445 and CHEM_V 449.

prerequisite.raw: Students will have completed their Year 3 laboratory requirements as outlined in their specialization

CHEM 449.prerequisiteText: Students will have completed their Year 3 laboratory requirements as outlined in their specialization

CHEM 460.title: Organic Synthesis: A Mechanistic Approach
CHEM 460.description: Presentation, mechanistic discussion and analysis of modern synthetic methods using principles of physical organic chemistry.

CHEM 461.title: Synthetic Chemical Biology
CHEM 461.description: Synthetic, mechanistic, and biochemical approaches to chemical biology, including the design of drugs, probes, and catalysts. .

CHEM 473.title: Structure Determination and Reaction Analysis
CHEM 473.description: Application of mass spectrometry and modern spectroscopic techniques, including multidimensional NMR spectroscopy, to reaction analysis and detailed characterization of complex organic and organometallic molecular structures.
CHEM 473.prerequisiteText: CHEM 245 and one of CHEM 313, CHEM 318, CHEM 330

CHEM 488.title: Topics in Chemistry
CHEM 488.description: Selected topics in a specific area of Chemistry. May be taken more than once for credit with permission of the Department.

prerequisite.raw: Third-year standing in a Chemistry specialization and permission of the Department

CHEM 488.prerequisiteText: Third-year standing in a Chemistry specialization and permission of the Department

CHEM 498.title: Co-operative Work Placement III
CHEM 498.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Taken during the summer following fourth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Chemistry.

CHEM 499.title: Co-operative Work Placement IV
CHEM 499.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Taken during the fall term of the fifth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Chemistry.

CHEM 501.title: Applications of Quantum Mechanics in Chemistry

CHEM 502.title: Advanced Physical Chemistry of the Solid State

CHEM 503.title: Equilibrium Statistical Mechanics in Chemistry
CHEM 503.description: Introductory principles of Statistical Mechanics with illustrations of chemical importance. Applications to molecular gases, liquids, solids, independent particle statistics, electric and magnetic moments, radiation, chemical equilibrium and reaction rates.

CHEM 507.title: Topics in Physical and Theoretical Chemistry

CHEM 508.title: Chemical Kinetics and Reaction Dynamics
CHEM 508.description: Macroscopic and microscopic kinetics; transition state theory; collision theory and reaction cross section, energy distributions, molecular beams and experimental techniques.

CHEM 513.title: Surface Chemistry
CHEM 513.description: Chemistry of the solid-gas interface: Modern methods for investigation of the structure of solid surfaces and interactions between solid surfaces and gases. Theory of adsorption, surface reactivity, and heterogeneous catalysis.

CHEM 514.title: Crystal Structures
CHEM 514.description: Crystal structures and structural analysis by the methods of X-ray diffraction and neutron diffraction.

CHEM 526.title: Bioinorganic Chemistry
CHEM 526.description: Inorganic aspects of biological chemistry; emphasis on the role of metal ions and metalloenzymes.

CHEM 529.title: Structural Methods in Inorganic Chemistry
CHEM 529.description: NMR, ESR, mass spectrometry, photoelectron spectroscopy (Auger, UV, X-Ray), Mossbauer spectroscopy, electrochemistry.

CHEM 548.title: Research Conference
CHEM 548.description: Attendance is compulsory for all graduate students in each year of registration for the M.Sc. or Ph.D. in chemistry. No credit value.

CHEM 560.title: Organic Chemistry: Building Molecules and Understanding Reactivity

CHEM 563.title: Advanced Physical Organic Chemistry
CHEM 563.description: Discussion of acidity functions, photochemistry and reactive intermediates in organic chemistry. Applications of molecular orbital theory to organic systems.

CHEM 566.title: Advanced Organic Synthesis
CHEM 566.description: Discussion of modern synthetic methods and applications to the synthesis of complex organic molecules.

CHEM 573.title: Application of Spectroscopy to Organic Structural Determinations
CHEM 573.description: A problem solving course to illustrate the application of NMR, mass spectrometry, ORD, CD, etc. to elucidation of structures of organic and organometallic compounds.
